items.headline: Parliament sets up committee on July 1983 riots
items.summary: Speaker Jagath Wickramaratne has appointed a special select committee, chaired by Minister Saroja Paulraj, to examine the Black July riots of 1983 and ways to foster communal harmony.

items.headline: President rejects salary protests, pledges Rs. 150bn in 2028 Budget
items.summary: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake described public sector pay protests as a coordinated bid to create a crisis and promised Rs. 150 billion for salaries and allowances in the 2028 Budget. He also flagged plans to raise the income threshold for the 36% tax band to Rs. 500,000 a month.

items.headline: Govt aims to restore credit rating to earlier levels after S&P upgrade
items.summary: Finance Ministry Secretary Harshana Suriyapperuma said the government hopes to return Sri Lanka's rating to its previous level following S&P's upgrade, but gave no timeline given geopolitical and climate risks.

items.headline: Russia agrees to help return 10 Sri Lankan fugitives
items.summary: Russia's Prosecutor General Alexandr Gutsan agreed to facilitate the handover of about 10 suspects believed to be in Russia, after talks with Justice Minister Harshana Nanayakkara; the two sides also signed a crime-cooperation agreement.

items.headline: Landslide warnings for 7 districts
items.summary: The NBRI issued Level 1 warnings for Badulla, Kalutara, Kandy, Kegalle, Matale, Nuwara Eliya and Ratnapura until 9 PM today, with Level 2 alerts for Udadumbara, Walapane, Nildandahinna and Hanguranketha.

items.headline: Poddala Jayantha responds to Gotabaya's court testimony
items.summary: Exiled journalist Poddala Jayantha disputed former President Gotabaya Rajapaksa's testimony in the Lalith-Kugan case that he did not know him, alleging past threats and his later abduction and assault.

items.headline: Sri Lanka urges stronger IORA cooperation
items.summary: At the IORA ministerial meeting in New Delhi, Foreign Minister Vijitha Herath called for practical cooperation on maritime safety, fisheries, disaster preparedness and the blue economy.

items.headline: O/L tuition classes banned from December 2
items.summary: Tuition classes, seminars and lectures for the 2026 G.C.E. O/L exam are banned from midnight on December 2 until the exam, which runs December 8–17 at 3,519 centres.

items.headline: Police fire on robbery suspects' van in Eheliyagoda
items.summary: Police shot at a fleeing van carrying robbery suspects in Parakaduwa, Eheliyagoda; one wounded suspect was arrested while others escaped.

items.headline: Constable deported from Dubai detained over T-56 case
items.summary: A police constable accused of handing his official T-56 rifle to a criminal gang and of drug trafficking was detained for 72 hours of questioning after being deported from Dubai.

items.headline: Navy seizes suspected drug vessel, arrests 7 foreigners
items.summary: The Navy intercepted a stateless vessel south of Dondra and brought it and seven foreign crew to Dikkowita harbour; the drug haul has not yet been disclosed.

items.headline: Heavy rain above 100mm expected in several provinces
items.summary: The Met Department forecasts heavy showers exceeding 100mm in parts of several provinces, adding to landslide risk in hill districts.

items.headline: Thurstan win on first innings
items.summary: Thurstan College beat Gurukula MV Kelaniya on first innings in an Under-19 schools match, with Rison Jansen scoring 81.

items.headline: Two Sri Lankan workers killed in South Korea
items.summary: Two Sri Lankan men in their 30s were killed in Hwaseong when cargo protruding from a passing truck struck them as they walked home from work; police are taking legal action against the driver.
